title: Fourier expansion of coordinate projection
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set with decidable equality. Suppose $B$ is a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function at an index $0_B$ and is orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, a set of coordinates $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, a function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and $x\in\Omega^n$, the expectation of $f$ after replacing the coordinates in $J$ of an independent sample from $\pi^n$ by those of $x$ is $\sum_{a:\,\operatorname{supp}(a)\subseteq J}\widehat f(a)\,\psi_a(x)$, where $\operatorname{supp}(a)=\{i:a_i\ne 0_B\}$, $\widehat f(a)=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi^n}[f(y)\psi_a(y)]$, and $\psi_a(x)=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}B_{a_i}(x_i)$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite nonempty basis index set $\iota$ with decidable equality
A basis vector is constant one at index $0_B$
Basis is orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$
